directions.rationale:
EDITORIAL / "auction catalogue" direction. The Card Doc reads like a collector magazine or an auction house's lot book, not a toy shop. Every real card photo is shown as a museum or auction lot: on a soft warm seamless backdrop (a radial gradient from ivory to stone with faint grain), with a long soft shadow and a placard caption underneath (card name in serif, then the detail in tracked mono). Where a photo came cut out on white (the Mantle glove pair, the Mantle in hand, the Garchomp corner), it uses mix-blend-mode: multiply, so the white disappears and the gloved hands seem to float on the seamless. That makes our small set of photos look shot in a studio. Charmander sits on a dark seamless so the result plates alternate light and dark.

How it stays different from Mint Workshop:
- **Colour:** warm ivory and stone with near-black ink. Mint uses sage, paper and red. Our one action colour is "Glove Blue" #2742D0, taken from the blue nitrile glove in our own Mantle photo, so the accent comes from our work.
- **Type:** Instrument Serif display (big, condensed, with italics for emphasis), Schibsted Grotesk for body and UI, IBM Plex Mono for labels. Mint uses Poppins all-caps with a script accent.
- **Buttons:** soft pill buttons with a blue glow shadow, instead of hard offset shadows.
- **Ticker:** serif words alternating roman and italic, with small blue diamond markers. Mint uses solid, outline and fade words with red dots.
- **Proof and closing:** reviews as typeset pull quotes plus a ruled Charizard "lot sheet" ($400 / PSA 10 / $2,500), instead of stickers. The page closes on a dark panel with a photo, not a red panel.

Principles taken from the study (not the look):
- Photos in about two of every three screens.
- The drag slider is the hero proof.
- One section pattern: eyebrow, short serif headline, lead paragraph on the right.
- Three alternating surfaces (ivory, stone, inset night panels with rounded corners).
- A call to action every one to two screens.
- A sticky header with "Book a Restoration".
- Prices large, in the action colour.
- Honesty kept close to the proof: the "We never" list sits in the hero and again in a dark box with the "Results vary" line.
- Body text at 15.5–17px and labels at 11–12.5px, with AA contrast.
- The hero headline (124px) clearly outranks the section headlines (92px).
- Motion is expo-out, short and quiet. All of it turns off under reduced motion, and the marquees then become static wrapped lists.

Wording: copied word for word from the inventory (TAGLINE, HERO headline, CARD_KINDS, FIXES, RESULTS captions, REVIEWS with "Repeat customer", TRUSTED_BY, SERVICE_CARDS with their em dashes, the tier table and bulk note, the how-it-works intro and six step titles, PROCESS methods, never and honesty, REASONS, the 5 FAQs, TOS_HIGHLIGHTS and the "Important:" paragraph, the closing lines, and the footer labels). The only new words are the approved "We do all cards." and "Watch the work". Index numbers (01–11) and BEFORE/AFTER tags are decoration only.

Logo: I did NOT use /card-doctor.jpg. It is a frame from the Pokémon anime. CLAUDE.md bans Pokémon characters and screenshots, and the inventory marks it "Do not use in the redesign", which outrank the computed task's instruction. Instead it has a tidy round double-ring frame with an italic serif "CD" monogram next to a serif "The Card Doc" wordmark. The frame is ready to take an owner-supplied mark later.

Photos used (copied or cropped into /tmp/directions/editorial/img/):
- Mantle specimens before and after (slider).
- The Mantle composite with the red arrow cropped off, as a full-width diptych plus split before and after crops.
- mantle-in-hand and mantle-detail.
- Charmander with the Pokémon-style "Before → After" lettering cropped off, plus an after-only crop.
- The Garchomp corner.
- Four DM screenshots with no names or avatars (testimonials 1, 3, 4, 6) as a "receipts" row.

How the review went: three screenshot passes, each at 1440x900 and 390x844.
- **Pass 1:** multiply blending was broken by z-index stacking contexts; the diptych was too tall; the receipts row was ragged; the Prep card repeated the Charmander composite; one eyebrow was wrong.
- **Pass 2:** the six steps had uneven columns and "Step-by-Step" broke at the hyphen; on mobile the slider sat below the CTAs; the Kits price wrapped awkwardly.
- **Pass 3:** reordered the mobile hero so the slider comes right after the headline. There is no horizontal overflow at either width.

Known limits:
- We only have about 4 distinct card photos, so Mantle and Charmander appear several times. The layout is built for the owner's 8–12 before/after pairs and reel covers to drop in.
- The DIY Kits card uses a typographic panel because there are no kit photos in the repo.
- In production the tier table must render from getLiveTiers().

directions.rationale:
Design read: a premium home page for collectors, with a hands-on workshop and lab-bench feel, led by real card photos. Dials: variance 7, motion 5, density 4.

The idea: the Card Doc bench. The page switches between three surfaces. Light "bench paper" holds the reading sections, a concrete mid-tone holds the photo sections, and a dark self-healing "cutting mat" (CSS grid lines on a 24/120px pitch, one faint 45-degree line, and ruler ticks along the edges) holds the proof and action sections. The single action colour is "glove cobalt" #2443e6, taken from the blue nitrile glove in our own Mantle photo, so the brand colour comes straight out of our proof photo. This is a different hue family from Mint's sage and tomato red.

The type is all our own: Archivo in a semi-condensed heavy cut for display, Instrument Sans for body text, and JetBrains Mono for spec and caption labels, which gives the workshop "spec label" voice. None of Mint's Poppins, Yellowtail or Inter Tight is used.

Buttons press down like keys: an inset bottom edge that drops 2px when pressed, not Mint's hard offset sticker shadow. Corners use one 4px radius everywhere; only chips are pills.

Photo-led:
- The hero puts the Mantle drag slider on the cutting mat, which bleeds off the right edge of the viewport. Two tilted "prints" sit beside it (Mantle in the blue glove, Charmander after), so the first screen is real cards.
- "We do all cards." has three tilted photo plates that straighten on hover.
- Results is an asymmetric bento: the large Mantle black-glove/blue-glove pair, a dark stat block, the Charmander pair, the Garchomp corner, and a Free Photo Review tile over the cracked Mantle detail.
- Watch the work has four 9:16 reel tiles.
- Services rows each carry a thumbnail.
- Process has a sticky photo beside it.
- The closing section is a full-height photo split.

Honesty and process lead in the middle of the page: the 5 methods, "We never", the risk line in a solid cobalt panel, then the 6-step rail and Why collectors choose us.

Fixes over Mint:
- The hero headline is clearly bigger than the section headlines.
- Body text is at least 15.5px and labels at least 11.5px, with AA contrast.
- There are no empty buttons.
- No photo is repeated more than needed.

Wording: all visible copy is the owner's, word for word, including em dashes, which the owner rule keeps over the taste skill's ban. The only new words are the approved "We do all cards." and "Watch the work", plus functional labels: Before/After, card names as captions, and "Reel".

Iterations:
1. First build. It had broken image aspect ratios (height attributes without height:auto), the reveal transform overriding the plate rotations, and a Charmander print covering the slider.
2. Fixed those. Tightened the hero so the slider shows in the first viewport. Gave Results a proper bento. Changed the duplicated "Behind the restoration" tile into Free Photo Review. Changed the closing photo.
3. Moved service photos into the rows. Fixed the 400px phone overflow (header) and the rail URL overflow. Hid DM screenshots on phones to shorten the page. Kept prices from wrapping.

Open items:
- Logo: the task said to use /card-doctor.jpg in a tidy frame, so it appears as a 44px square crop of the face in a white mat frame. The inventory (section 1c) flags this image as a Pokémon-anime frame (Nintendo/TPC IP) that should be replaced with a wordmark. The frame is built so a monogram can drop in without a layout change.
- Reels use existing photos as covers until real reel covers exist. The fourth cover uses the Mantle pair, not the Charmander image with Pokémon-style lettering.
- Dark-mode tokens are not split out yet, because the page relies on its fixed light/mat rhythm.
- Reduced motion turns off the marquees, reveals and drop-ins and wraps the ticker.
- The slider supports drag, arrow keys (Shift for steps of 10), Home and End.

directions.rationale:
Direction name: "Hobby Shop Poster". It aims for the energy of a card-show booth: saturated cobalt and wax-pack yellow blocks, condensed sports-style headlines, die-cut sticker labels, and real card photos treated as physical objects. The photos are white-bordered prints, rotated with layered soft shadows, and the hero Mantle sits in a translucent acrylic one-touch holder (glare streak, corner screws). That holder replaces Mint's playmat-and-card-slot idea with something every collector owns.

How it stays clear of The Mint Workshop's signatures:
- Different hue family: cobalt, ink navy and yellow instead of sage, cream and tomato red.
- Different type: Big Shoulders Display and Schibsted Grotesk instead of Poppins, Yellowtail and Inter Tight.
- No hard 4px offset shadows. Buttons are pills with a white die-cut edge and a soft shadow.
- No starbursts or ribbon, no prohibition-sign callout, no three-colour headline.
- The symptoms band is a single tilted yellow tape with small cobalt card shapes between the words, not their solid/outline/fade marquee.

What it borrows from the study is the principles: photos in most screens, proof in several formats (slider, big before/after print, Charmander composite, close-up texture tile, reels, case-study stickers, stats), colour alternation every section (cobalt, yellow, chalk, ink, chalk, cobalt, chalk, ink, white, chalk, white, yellow, ink footer), and a call to action every one to two screens.

Copy and assets:
- All wording is verbatim from the inventory, page.tsx, how-it-works, lib/reviews.ts and lib/trusted-by.ts. Owner em dashes are kept. The only new words are the approved "We do all cards." and "Watch the work", plus one decorative sticker on the photo fan ("Vintage or modern"), which is a fragment of the owner's own FAQ line.
- Only real photos are used. Crops were made from public/ (the Mantle composite cut below the red arrow, the Charmander composite cut below the Pokémon-style lettering, Garchomp flattened onto white) and saved in /tmp/directions/bold-graphic/img/.
- The logo is /card-doctor.jpg, cropped to the head inside a rounded-square ink frame, as the task asked.

Flags for the owner:
- The inventory marks card-doctor.jpg as a frame from the Pokémon anime (Nintendo IP). It is still the brand mark in PRODUCT.md, so it is used here, but it should be swapped for an owned mark before launch.
- The reel covers are placeholders, as in lib/reels.ts.

Iterations, three screenshot passes at 1440x900 and 390x844:
- Pass 1: hero headline ran to 4 lines and pushed "We never" below the fold; reel covers did not fill their 9:16 frames; a "Trusted by" heading overflow; the Charizard case sat beside an unrelated Garchomp thumb; the closing headline ran to 5 lines; prices were uppercased; the four Terms cards looked templated; horizontal overflow from the tilted ticker.
- Pass 1 fixes: headline goes full width on 2 lines with the copy and the holder below it; reel frames set to block display; Trusted by gets a fixed column; the case moved under the Charmander proof; the stats row now has 5000+, Free and a full-bleed close-up of the cracked Mantle; prices keep the owner's case; Terms became an open 2x2 with rules; overflow-x is clipped.
- Pass 2: sticker and print placement moved off the headline and the AFTER label.

Accessibility:
- The slider is draggable with the pointer and has a role=slider handle with arrow and Home/End keys.
- The FAQ uses native details/summary.
- Focus rings are yellow.
- Under reduced motion all animation is removed: load float-in, slider wipe intro and both marquees.

Not done:
- The mock has no dark mode, since the page already alternates light and dark blocks.
- Two marquees stay (trust strip and symptoms ticker) because the owner requires both; they are styled very differently.

- h-md clamp(36px, 4.2vw, 60px).
- Card h3 26-40px Big Shoulders 800-900.
- Lead clamp(17px, 1.5vw, 20px), line-height 1.55, 56ch max.
- Body 17px (16px on mobile), line-height 1.6.
- Eyebrow 18px Big Shoulders 800, tracking .06em, uppercase. Used twice on the page.
- Buttons 15-17px, weight 800.

Spacing:
- Container 1280px; gutter clamp(20px, 4vw, 40px).
- Section padding clamp(72px, 9vw, 128px).
- Grid gaps 20-28px for cards, 56-72px between split columns.
- Header height 74px desktop, 64px mobile.

Radii rule:
- Photos and prints 8px (inner image 3px), the card-corner feel.
- Panels and tiles 22px.
- Review cards 14px; acrylic holder 18px; icon tiles 12px.
- Buttons and the Instagram chip: full pill.
- Stickers: die-cut 6px rectangles.

Shadows:
- Print: 0 1px 1px rgba(8,12,40,.18), 0 10px 18px -8px rgba(8,12,40,.35), 0 34px 60px -26px rgba(8,12,40,.55).
- Print on dark: same layers at .4/.55/.7 black.
- Sticker and yellow button: 0 0 0 3px #fff die-cut edge plus 0 8-10px 16-22px -8px rgba(8,12,40,.5).
- Holder: inset white edge plus 0 26px 40px -14px and 0 60px 90px -40px navy.
- No zero-blur offset shadows.

Texture:
- 16px halftone dot field (white at .14-.16) masked to a soft radial, on cobalt surfaces only.

Motion (easing cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)):
- Hero load: holder rises 1.1s; back prints fly in at 0.25s and 0.38s; sticker pops at 1.15s; the slider wipes from 18% to 50% between 1.0s and 2.6s.
- Hovers: button lift 0.18s (-2px, arrow nudges 3px); print and reel lift 0.45s; FAQ plus rotates 45deg in 0.3s.
- Marquees: trust strip 38s and symptoms ticker 44s, both linear; the trust strip pauses on hover.
- prefers-reduced-motion: everything is static.

Icons: lucide paths in an inline sprite, stroke 1.75.

11. **Why collectors choose us (white).** Left: the cracked Mantle close-up with the restored Mantle print and a "30+ years of combined collecting" sticker. Right: H2, lead, and the four reasons with icon tiles.

scores.notes: Closest to Mint's quality bar without copying its look. The first desktop screen is real cards: the Mantle slider sits on the cutting mat, which bleeds off the right edge, with tilted Mantle-in-glove and Charmander prints beside it. 'We do all cards' has three white-bordered prints on a concrete mid-tone. Results is a real bento: the big glove pair, a dark 5000+/30+ stat block, the Charmander pair, the Garchomp corner and a Free Photo Review tile. The four 9:16 reels sit on a light ground with clear captions. Service rows carry thumbnails, the process section has a sticky photo, and the page closes on a full-height photo split. Sticky header with Track Order and Book a Restoration, with a CTA every 1-2 screens. Weaknesses: Archivo heavy plus cobalt plus Instrument Sans is competent but slightly generic, and in places it reads like a SaaS template. The cutting-mat grid is so faint it barely registers, which is its whole signature. The Mantle in-glove photo appears 6+ times (hero print, We do all cards, Results, reels, Behind the restoration, closing). The Charizard case strikes through $400, which reads as a discount price. There is no tier table or price cards anywhere (grep finds no 'Bronze'), while Mint's 'Priced by your card's value' band is one of its strongest converters. The Free Photo Review tile sits on a muddy, dimmed Mantle detail. The Terms block is four icon-in-box cards, which looks templated. The logo is the anime card-doctor.jpg crop, which is banned. Mobile: a ticker plus a cramped header (logo, filled CTA and menu at 390px), and the slider falls into the second screen. The testimonial masonry becomes 9 stacked cards, about 3 screens of text. The DIY Kits row uses a DM screenshot as its 'thumbnail'.

The most distinctive and the most 'luxury': ivory and stone seamless backdrops, Instrument Serif with italic blue emphasis, mono placards, and multiply-blended cutouts. The Charmander on a dark plate and the Mantle-in-glove floating on the seamless both look studio-shot. The ruled Charizard lot sheet ($400 / PSA 10 / $2,500) and the giant serif 'The Card Doc' footer wordmark are excellent. It is the only mock with a real tier table (Bronze to Fast Pass, with the 'Most popular' and 'Front of queue' chips). It correctly avoids the anime logo with a CD monogram. The mobile hero order is right: headline, then the slider in the first screen. Weaknesses: it is too quiet for what the user asked for ('looks amazing with pictures, like the mint workshop'). The hero slider is a small framed tile on the right with lots of empty ivory. Several desktop screens are mostly air: the 5000+/Free stat row, the 'Proven Results' intro and the Terms intro. Photo density is lower than Mint's 9 of 15 frames. The CTAs are small soft pills that disappear, and the action colour is used sparingly, so conversion pull is weak. Light serif body and tiny 11px mono labels hurt scannability. Reviews are a long wall of serif quotes. The 'Trusted by' band on mobile is a big empty stone panel with a heading. Overall it is beautiful but reads as an auction catalogue rather than an energetic hobby brand.

The most energetic, and the one-touch acrylic holder around the hero slider is the single best new idea across all three. White-bordered tilted prints, the yellow tape ticker with card-shaped separators, die-cut sticker chips, Trusted-by cards with follower counts and Instagram tags, and big yellow step numerals all have hobby-shop charm. Weaknesses: cobalt and yellow full-bleed blocks with condensed all-caps sports type and sticker labels are noisy and drift toward a kids' toy-shop / Mint-adjacent sticker vibe (originality is lowest: sticker badges and a tilted ticker are close to Mint's signature). It does not feel premium enough for $2,500 cards. The testimonial cards on blue look like generic white SaaS cards, and the long wall of them goes on and on. 'Services' has a large blue Restoration tile next to a cramped Prep tile, which is unbalanced. The closing yellow panel is busy, with prints clipped at the edges. It uses card-doctor.jpg (anime IP) as the logo. There is no tier table. Mobile: the first screen is all type with no photo (the holder starts in the second screen). The testimonials scroll sideways with half-cut cards, and the condensed all-caps step titles wrap awkwardly ('ARRIVAL, CHECK- IN, AND EVALUATION').

Use it on the light 'We do all cards' and Results tiles instead of flat white mats.

Better still, make it a price-card band in the action colour on the cutting mat, like Mint's 'Priced by your card's value' strip, since the workshop mock has no prices beyond 'From $75 / card'.

From editorial: the giant 'The Card Doc' wordmark across the bottom of the footer, and the CD monogram in place of the anime card-doctor.jpg.

scores.notes: The most refined and most clearly different from Mint: ivory and stone surfaces, Instrument Serif with blue italics, and the multiply-blended Mantle glove pair floating on a seamless backdrop all look studio-shot. The serif card-kinds list with superscript numbers is a lovely detail. Weaknesses: it is quiet and cool for an Instagram thumb. Thin serif at 15-17px on stone reads faint on a phone, and the page feels like a magazine rather than a shop with a line out the door. The desktop hero slider is small, about 300px wide inside a padded plate, so the proof does not dominate. The mobile header has no Book button (just a cart and a menu), so a phone visitor has no CTA in reach for long stretches. The 'Watch the work' dark panel is mostly empty in its first frame. The services cards and the tier table are text-led and small. The page is long on mobile (24 frames) and the testimonials alone take about 3 screens. It gets credit for a mobile hero that puts the slider straight after the headline and for not using the anime logo.

The most conversion-sound build: a persistent 'Book a Restoration' button sits in the mobile header on every frame, 'We never' is in the hero, prices are large in cobalt, there are CTAs every 1-2 screens, and the results bento (Mantle pair, 5000+/30+ stat block, Charmander, Garchomp, Free Photo Review tile) is the best proof section of the three. The cutting-mat texture is a smart, owned idea. But the overall look is the most generic: square blue SaaS buttons, heavy grotesk on grey, outlined secondary buttons. It reads as 'competent template', not 'amazing'. The mobile hero pushes the slider below the first screen: you see the headline, two buttons and the never-list first. The testimonial cards stack into roughly 3 screens of plain white boxes. The logo uses the card-doctor.jpg anime frame (an IP problem). Services is only two rows with small thumbnails, and DIY Kits disappears into a dark tile. The tilted prints in 'We do all cards' are nice.

The strongest thumb-stopper, and the closest to the energy the user loved in Mint. Saturated cobalt and yellow blocks, condensed sports type and real cards shown as physical white-bordered prints. The hero Mantle in an acrylic one-touch holder is the single best photo idea across all three. Photos appear in nearly every frame: the fanned prints in 'We do all cards', the Proven Results prints, a Charizard stat case, reels, and a Services bento with photos in the Restoration and Prep tiles. The yellow pill CTAs on cobalt are unmissable, and mobile is the shortest (19 frames) with big tap targets. Problems: (1) the hero slider labels are wrong or clipped. 'AF' sits top-left over the damaged half and 'BEFORE' top-right over the restored half, and on desktop the '5000+ CARDS RESTORED' sticker crowds the headline. (2) It uses the card-doctor.jpg anime logo. (3) Originality is the weakest: the stickers, tilted ticker tape and colour-blocking echo Mint's playful-sticker grammar even though the hues differ. (4) Cobalt on cobalt sections with white cards (reviews) gets loud and same-y. The yellow 'Important' box and the yellow closing panel risk looking cheap rather than trustworthy for cards worth $5,000. (5) The mobile hero shows no photo in the first 844px, only the headline, CTAs and the never chips. The holder appears only on frame 2. (6) The testimonials on mobile become a horizontal row that is clipped with no swipe cue.
